reply_text:
**Don't merge this yet. The main feature doesn't work.** `mergeImports` doesn't remove overlapping contacts. The tests pass, but they don't test the case that matters.

**Blocker: `dedupe` compares objects, not ids** (`src/dedupe.js`)
`[...new Set(contacts)]` only drops a contact if it's the exact same object in memory. Your README says an overlapping import produces a separate object with the same id, so `Set` keeps both copies. I ran it to check:

```
mergeImports([{id:1,name:'Ada'}], [{id:1,name:'Ada'},{id:2}])
→ [{id:1,name:'Ada'}, {id:1,name:'Ada'}, {id:2}]   // id 1 appears twice
```

This needs to dedupe by `id` and keep the first one seen, as the README says. For example, track seen ids in a `Set` and filter the list with it.

**Tests don't catch it** (`test/dedupe.test.js`)
The "same object is not repeated" test passes `[a, a]`, which is the one case where comparing objects happens to work. You need a test with two different objects that share an id, e.g. `dedupe([{id:1,name:'Ada'},{id:1,name:'Ada B'}])` should give back only the first. A test for `mergeImports` with lists that actually overlap would also help, since `merge.js` has no tests right now.

**Minor**
- `byName` is fine. It copies the list before sorting, so the input stays untouched, and contacts without a name don't crash it. Contacts with no name sort first, since they're treated as `''`. Make sure that's what you want.
- Nothing in the app calls `byName` yet, and `mergeImports` doesn't sort. That's fine if you meant it that way.
- The version bump to 2.2.0 and the changelog entry look good.

The test suite passes as it stands, so CI won't flag any of this.
